title: E-LDA: Toward Interpretable LDA Topic Models with Strong Guarantees in Logarithmic Parallel Time
venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2025), PMLR 267
task: MAP inference of document-topic assignments in LDA with guarantees
problem: No practical LDA algorithm has provable guarantees for document-topic assignment, which social-science and causal-inference uses depend on.
architecture: Casts LDA MAP assignment under sparsity constraints as monotone submodular maximisation over topic-document links; fast serial greedy and parallel adaptive-sampling algorithms reach a near-optimal (1-1/e) solution in logarithmic parallel time; candidate topics generated from coherence functions (co-occurrence, exp-UMass) so each topic is tied to a keyword; out-of-sample objective preserves independence (SUTVA) for causal inference with topics as treatments.
key_results: Higher log posterior than Gibbs in all 90 runs with the same topics and sparsity (e.g. Congress -1.78 vs -2.05, x10^6; p < 10^-10).
Co-occurrence and exp-UMass E-LDA solutions give 2.53-4.20 and 1.18-1.67 times better mean coherence than Gibbs topics (5 top words).
Serial research code runs in 2-3 seconds.
strengths: First practical LDA inference with approximation guarantees and logarithmic adaptivity.
Keyword-anchored, interpretable topics and validity for causal inference designs.

limitations.text: Topic quality judged mainly by UMass coherence (with candidate topics generated from coherence-type functions); no human evaluation.
Focuses on LDA with sparsity constraints; other variants are only argued to generalise.

notes: Authors report that a plain UMass generator performs relatively poorly, arguing coherence gains are not only an artefact.
